Summarize Brown Heart Assistant..answer: The Brown Heart Assistant (BHAI) is a full‑stack, citation‑grounded health‑education platform that Pranav built from scratch for the Joshi Health Foundation, now serving more than 5,000 users and complemented by a searchable FAQ site [1].  It uses a router‑orchestrated multi‑agent architecture that routes queries to specialized agents (FAQ, MASALA Study, Instagram, YouTube, movie‑timestamp) and applies source‑grounded prompts, confidence gating, and a “refuse‑and‑route” safety design for medical questions [2][1].  Retrieval is hybrid, combining BM25, Azure PostgreSQL/pgvector, HNSWlib, and NVIDIA embeddings with reciprocal‑rank‑fusion, and the chat generation is streamed via Azure OpenAI [3].  Low‑confidence medical queries trigger a human‑in‑the‑loop (HITL) escalation tool that matches doctors by specialty, contacts clinicians, or books appointments [3].  The production backend includes Azure Blob artifact hydration, checksum validation, signed sessions, admin health checks, environment‑based model configuration, LangSmith tracing across agent runs and retrieval scores, and a suite of 113 passing tests to ensure reliability [3][4].

citations.title: RAG Reliability & Audits
citations.snippet: Pranav approaches RAG reliability by building self-correcting architectures. In projects like Agentic Graph-RAG (The Brain) and Brown Heart Assistant, he ensures high reliability using query analysis, hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vector matching), Neo4j knowledge graphs, multi-step evidence sufficiency audits, confidence gating thresholds, and medical-safety refusal filters to prevent hallucinations.

How does he approach RAG reliability?.answer: Pranav tackles RAG reliability by designing self‑correcting architectures that continuously audit and refine their own retrieval results. He combines query analysis with hybrid retrieval—mixing dense vector search (FAISS/Pinecone) and classic BM25—while grounding the data in large Neo4j knowledge graphs, then runs multi‑step evidence‑sufficiency audits and applies confidence‑gating thresholds plus safety‑refusal filters to block hallucinations [1]. In his Agentic Graph‑RAG (The Brain) system, a LangGraph agent automatically expands failed queries using HyDE, pulls supplemental web/Wikipedia data via Tavily, verifies supporting snippets, and reranks results with cross‑encoders, which together lifted the hit rate from 82 % to 92 % and faithfulness from 0.708 to 0.847 [2][3].

citations.title: Agentic Graph-RAG: The Brain
citations.snippet: Pranav built 'Agentic Graph-RAG: The Brain', a self-correcting LangGraph agent that audits evidence sufficiency, expands searches to web/Wikipedia via Tavily when needed, verifies supporting snippets, and refines failed queries with HyDE query expansion before answering. It uses hybrid retrieval across FAISS/Pinecone dense vectors, BM25, and a 311K-node / 374K-edge Neo4j knowledge graph over 39K chunks, unified with NVIDIA and Cross-Encoder reranking. On 100 judged SQuAD-style examples it improved retrieval hit rate from 82% to 92% and LLM-judged faithfulness from 0.708 to 0.847.
